entries.reason: the class is what an application uses to place and take VoIP calls; iOS 6.1.3 has no PushKit-shaped registration surface, but its own apsd already hands out a real device token through -[UIApplication registerForRemoteNotificationTypes:], so this port bridges to it rather than answering with a fake or absent token
entries.effect: initWithQueue: gives a real instance; setDesiredPushTypes: containing PKPushTypeVoIP delivers a cached token immediately if one is held, and re-asks apsd for a token when the application has already registered any UIUserNotificationType through registerUserNotificationSettings:; pushTokenForType: reads the same cache; a delegate that answers pushRegistry:didUpdatePushCredentials:forType: is called on the registry's queue whenever the application's own -application:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken: fires, reached by chaining onto the application delegate's class the first time -setDelegate: names it
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the contract; -[UIApplication registerForRemoteNotificationTypes:] and its delegate callbacks on iOS 6.1.3, exercised through the existing UIApplication+UserNotificationSettings.m backport

entries.reason: the class carries the token PKPushRegistry delivers; real independently of how the token was obtained
entries.effect: type and token hold what PKPushRegistry gave it
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the contract

entries.reason: the class is a strong-imported symbol risk for an application whose delegate method signatures name it, even though this port never constructs one: apsd on iOS 6.1.3 wakes no suspended application for any push, VoIP or otherwise, so there is no incoming push for PKPushRegistryDelegate to be handed
entries.effect: type and dictionaryPayload hold what is given to the (unused) initializer; no code path in this port ever calls pushRegistry:didReceiveIncomingPushWithPayload:forType:
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the contract

entries.reason: the constant a VoIP registration names; the value is the constant's own name, the form every PKPushType/PKPushSubtype string in Apple's documentation and headers back to iOS 8 takes, not measured in a shared cache since attempting to read the literal's bytes across the iOS 12.0 and 16.0 caches (modules/apple/dyld.lua's pointer_at chain-resolving the CFConstantString bytes pointer) kept landing outside every mapping - recorded as unresolved rather than guessed silently
entries.source: the constant's own name, unverified against the shared cache; see facts/PushKit/PushKit.md

entries.reason: the header marks -init unavailable and names -initWithQueue: as the designated initialiser, with nil documented to mean the main queue, so a registry made any other way is a registry on the main queue
entries.effect: returns -initWithQueue:nil, so [[PKPushRegistry alloc] init] gives the same registry the header's own nil describes: a real one, registered in the live set, delivering on the main queue
entries.source: the header of PKPushRegistry.h in SDK 26.2 for the contract (-init NS_UNAVAILABLE, -initWithQueue: NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER with nil documented as the main queue); the same answer the port gives +[UICollectionViewDiffableDataSource new], whose -init the header also marks unavailable
